rationale: scripts/audit/mcq-leakage.mts flagged step ch1's correct option ('9.1, since 83 is much closer to 82.81 (9.1^2) than to 84.64 (9.2^2)', 68 chars) as length-prose-vs-prose against the longest distractor (42 chars). REVIEWED AND KEPT, not edited: this challenge is explicitly a reasoning-comparison task ('A classmate's reasoning went wrong somewhere -- find the correct one'), and unlike the fn-0x-02 pair, all four options already carry parallel inline reasoning, not bare claims -- option b also uses 'since' (83 is closer to 100 than to 81), option d also uses 'since' (that's the whole-number bound), and option c states its own justification (the exact midpoint of 9.1 and 9.2). The correct option is longer specifically because the true reasoning requires citing BOTH tenths-level brackets (82.81 and 84.64) to justify which one 83 is closer to, whereas each wrong reason is simpler (and wrong) by construction -- comparing at the wrong scale, picking an arbitrary midpoint, or not narrowing at all. Shortening the correct label would mean deleting the actual mathematical justification the challenge exists to test, which is exactly the case scripts/audit/mcq-leakage.mts's own header comment carves out as requiring human misconception-family judgment rather than a mechanical rewrite ('the true reason is longer because the true reason IS longer... naming the two separately is what lets the first be worked now and the second be scheduled honestly'). No edit made. Independently re-verified the arithmetic by hand: 83 - 82.81 = 0.19, 84.64 - 83 = 1.64, 0.19 < 1.64, so 9.1 is correct.
